entries.sentence: The NHS says the first symptom most women notice is a lump or an area of thickened tissue in the breast.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page excerpt: first symptom most women notice is a lump or thickened area.

entries.sentence: Most breast lumps are not cancer, but a doctor still needs to check any new one.
entries.note: NHS: most breast lumps are not cancerous; should still be checked by a doctor.

entries.sentence: Other changes can include a different size or shape of the breast, fluid coming from the nipple, a lump or swelling in the armpit, and changes to the skin or nipple.
entries.note: NHS list: change in breast size or shape, nipple discharge, lump or swelling in either armpit, skin or nipple changes.

entries.sentence: Breast pain on its own is not usually a sign of breast cancer, and these changes can happen without any pain.
entries.note: NHS: breast pain is not usually a symptom of breast cancer; symptoms can occur without pain; NHS 111 Wales: pain that comes and goes is usually not a symptom.

entries.sentence: Pain linked to the menstrual cycle often affects both breasts and can feel dull, heavy or aching.
entries.note: NHS Shropshire, Telford and Wrekin page: cyclical pain dull, heavy or aching, affects both breasts.

entries.sentence: Pain in the breast or armpit that does not go away should also be checked, according to NHS 111 Wales.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales: pain in breast or armpit that does not go away should be checked.

entries.sentence: Ductal carcinoma starts in the milk ducts and is the most common type, while lobular carcinoma starts in the lobules.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Rarer types include inflammatory breast cancer.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Staging describes how large the cancer is and whether it has spread.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query. Staging = size and spread.

entries.sentence: Stages run from 0 to IV, and a higher stage means a more advanced cancer.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Stage 0 describes ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), where the cells have not spread beyond the wall of the duct into surrounding tissue.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Grades run from 1 to 3: grade 1 cells look the most like normal cells and are less likely to spread, while grade 3 cells look the most abnormal and are more likely to grow fast.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Laboratory tests on the biopsy sample also check hormone receptors and a protein called HER2, and these results help guide treatment.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query. Summary: hormone receptors and HER2 checked and guide treatment.

entries.sentence: NHS England guidance says people with suspected breast cancer should be seen in a one-stop clinic that can offer examination, mammography, ultrasound and biopsy on the same day.
entries.note: NHS England guidance excerpt: one-stop clinic with same-day access to clinical examination, mammography, ultrasound and biopsy.

entries.sentence: Several tests in one visit are called a triple assessment: a physical examination, imaging and, if needed, a biopsy.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query. Summary: typically one-stop clinic, several tests in one visit, also called triple assessment.

entries.sentence: A mammogram is an x-ray of the breast and is usually used for women over 40, while women under 40 are usually advised to have an ultrasound scan alone.
entries.note: Royal Marsden clinic page excerpt: over 40 usually mammogram; under 40 ultrasound alone normally advised.

entries.sentence: A biopsy takes a small sample of breast cells or tissue, and whether it is done depends on the examination and imaging results.
entries.note: Same page excerpt.

entries.sentence: Scan results are often given on the same day, while biopsy results need a further appointment.
entries.note: Same page excerpt: scan results same day; biopsy results at a further appointment.

entries.sentence: The results are discussed at a multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting, where specialists review them and recommend further tests or a treatment plan.
entries.note: Same page excerpt on MDT meeting.

entries.sentence: The NHS says treatment usually involves a combination of surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and, in some cases, hormone or biological therapies.
entries.note: NHS treatment page excerpt.

entries.sentence: A multidisciplinary team of specialists plans each person's treatment together.
entries.note: NHS: anyone diagnosed should be assigned an MDT.

entries.sentence: Surgery is generally the first step, and the operation depends on the type of cancer.
entries.note: NHS treatment page: surgery generally first, depends on type.

entries.sentence: A lumpectomy, also called a wide local excision, removes the area of cancer from the breast, and radiotherapy to the rest of the breast is usually given afterwards to lower the risk of the cancer coming back.
entries.note: CRUK lumpectomy page excerpt.

entries.sentence: The NHS describes breast-conserving surgery followed by radiotherapy as being as successful as removing the whole breast for early-stage breast cancer.
entries.note: NHS summary: breast-conserving surgery plus radiotherapy as successful as total mastectomy for early-stage disease.

entries.sentence: A sentinel lymph node biopsy removes a few lymph nodes from the armpit to check for spread.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Radiotherapy is often given after surgery to destroy any cancer cells that may remain.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Chemotherapy uses anti-cancer drugs and is sometimes given before surgery to shrink a cancer.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Hormone therapy is for cancers with hormone receptors; it lowers the levels of hormones such as oestrogen or blocks their effects.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK lists skin changes, tiredness and swelling as common short-term effects of radiotherapy, with heart and lung problems rarer and later.
entries.note: CRUK radiotherapy side effects page; summary: skin changes, tiredness, swelling; rarer longer-term heart damage and uncommon lung scarring.

entries.sentence: Chemotherapy side effects can include nausea, hair loss, tiredness and temporarily lowered blood counts, and most can be managed with medicines.
entries.note: Search summary blended several pages and did not name the page; attributed to the pages returned for the query.

entries.sentence: Hormone therapy side effects resemble the menopause, such as hot flushes and mood changes, and joint and muscle aches are common with aromatase inhibitors.
entries.note: CRUK hormone therapy page listed hot flushes, mood changes, painful joints; Breast Cancer Now: joint and muscle aches common with letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane.

entries.sentence: Cancer Research UK says these effects are often worst at the start and usually ease within weeks or months.
entries.note: CRUK: side effects often worst at the start; summary says usually ease within weeks or months.

entries.sentence: The Royal Marsden says people can feel more tired than usual for several months after treatment ends.
entries.note: Summary of Royal Marsden guidance on fatigue after treatment.

entries.sentence: Fatigue can come from the cancer itself and from surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and pacing activity and keeping a diary can help show when energy is higher.
entries.note: Summary of Royal Marsden self-help material.

entries.sentence: Breast Cancer Now says regular activity can help maintain or improve physical and mental health during and after treatment.
entries.note: Breast Cancer Now page excerpt.

entries.sentence: Lymphoedema is swelling caused by a build-up of fluid, and NHS Scotland says it typically begins within the first four years after breast cancer treatment.
entries.note: NHS Scotland pathway summary: swelling from fluid build-up; onset typically within first four years.

entries.sentence: People with lymphoedema can be referred to a specialist for advice on exercise, massage and skin care.
entries.note: Same page.

entries.sentence: Follow-up leaflets say worries about intimacy and relationships are common after treatment.
entries.note: Summary of NHS follow-up leaflet mentioning intimacy and relationship concerns.

entries.sentence: Secondary breast cancer, also called metastatic, advanced or stage 4 breast cancer, is breast cancer that has spread to another part of the body.
entries.note: Search summary of Breast Cancer Now and CRUK secondary pages.

entries.sentence: It can spread to places such as the bones, lungs, liver or brain, and it is the same type of cancer as the original.
entries.note: Same.

entries.sentence: It can appear years or sometimes months after the first cancer, and for some people it is found at the same time or before.
entries.note: Same.

entries.sentence: Sources say it usually cannot be cured, but treatment can often control it and ease symptoms.
entries.note: Summary: usually can't be cured but treatment can often control it and ease symptoms.

entries.sentence: Breast Cancer Now says the aims are to slow the spread, control the cancer and support wellbeing, using treatments such as chemotherapy, hormone therapy and targeted drugs.
entries.note: Summary: goal to slow the spread, control and support quality of life; common treatments chemo, hormone, targeted.

entries.sentence: As treatments have improved, more people are living longer after a diagnosis, Breast Cancer Now says.
entries.note: Summary: more and more people living longer.
